title: Wireframes/prototype for Console onboarding checklist (entry point, step detail drawer, deep links)
creator: Tessa Morgan
project: Guided onboarding + first production launch checklist
description:
Goal
Create wireframes and a clickable prototype for the Console onboarding checklist experience to support the Guided Onboarding + “First Production Launch” initiative.

This ticket covers:
- Checklist entry point placement and states (hidden/visible/complete)
- Step list patterns and status visual language
- Step detail drawer (content, deep links, acceptance criteria, troubleshooting)
- Deep-linking patterns (from checklist → relevant Console pages/docs; and from key pages → checklist)
- Empty/error/loading states (including event ingestion lag and permission issues)

Context
We’re adding an in-product checklist in the Redwood Console to reduce time-to-first-success (TTFS) and time-to-first-production (TTFP) and to deflect common onboarding tickets (401/403 auth mistakes, 429 rate limits, streaming disconnect confusion, usage dashboard lag).

Primary personas
- Self-serve engineer: wants fast first call + confidence about “what’s next”
- Team lead / platform engineer: wants production readiness steps, observability hooks, quotas/budgets, and rollout safety
- Support/CS (secondary): needs to interpret checklist state quickly during troubleshooting

Entry point (where checklist lives)
Proposed (MVP):
- Persistent “Getting started” module on Console home/dashboard for new tenants.
- Secondary entry point: left nav “Onboarding” item behind a feature flag (only for cohorts).
- Tertiary: deep link CTA on key pages (API Keys page, Usage/Quotas page) that returns to the checklist with context.

Key wireframe decisions
1) Checklist list view
- Each step row includes: status icon, step name, short 1-line description, CTA (“View details” / “Go to…”) and optional “Learn more” (docs).
- Statuses (MVP): Not started, In progress, Completed, Attention (blocked/warning). “Attention” is used sparingly (e.g., first 401/403 detected, first 429 detected, streaming disconnect detected) and routes user to relevant guidance.
- Ordering: keep “first call” steps above “production launch” steps. Avoid mixing “Console setup” and “SDK code changes” in a way that feels like busywork.

2) Step detail drawer
- Right-side drawer (preferred over modal to preserve context and allow quick switching steps).
- Standard structure:
  a) Step title + short why-it-matters sentence
  b) Completion criteria (explicit, scannable)
  c) Primary CTA (deep link into Console or code snippet docs)
  d) Troubleshooting accordion (top 2–3 known failures only)
  e) Optional “What good looks like” snippet (e.g., retries/timeouts defaults)
- Drawer supports “Next step” navigation to reduce back-and-forth.

3) Deep linking patterns
- “Go to API Keys” / “Go to Usage & Quotas” / “Go to Observability” CTAs deep link to Console pages.
- If user lands on a deep-linked Console page, show a lightweight inline banner: “This is step X in your onboarding checklist” with a link back (no full guided tour in MVP).
- Docs deep links always open in a new tab and use canonical URLs (avoid linking to transient PR previews).

4) Data/telemetry latency messaging
- Include a consistent “Data may take up to N minutes to appear” note on steps tied to telemetry/usage dashboards (to reduce confusion).
- If step completion depends on server-side events, show a neutral “Waiting for activity” state rather than implying user did something wrong.

5) Accessibility and content constraints
- All statuses have text equivalents; icon-only is not acceptable.
- Drawer content must be readable at 400% zoom without truncation.
- Step titles target ≤ 44 characters; descriptions target ≤ 90 characters (aligned with DES-427 copy guidelines).

Prototype & artifacts
- Figma file: https://figma.com/file/RI-Console/Onboarding-Checklist-Wireframes-DES-418
- Clickable prototype: https://figma.com/proto/RI-Console/Onboarding-Checklist-Prototype-DES-418
- Exported wireframe frames for eng review (PNG): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/RI-onboarding-checklist-wireframes-DES-418

Frames included (MVP)
1) Console Home (new tenant): checklist module with 6–10 steps
2) Checklist full-page view: step list with filter (All / Incomplete / Attention)
3) Step detail drawer: completed vs not started vs attention state variants
4) Empty state: checklist hidden for non-cohort / feature flag off
5) Error state: cannot load checklist progress (service unavailable)
6) Inline banner on deep-linked pages (API Keys, Usage)
7) Mobile-ish narrow layout sanity check (not fully responsive spec; just constraints)

Open questions (tracked for UX spec / product)
- Do we allow “dismiss checklist” for MVP, or only collapse? (Risk: users dismiss and lose value; Support requested persistent visibility.)
- How do we handle multi-user tenants where one user completed step(s)? Proposed: tenant-level checklist with “Last updated by” in drawer (but avoid listing emails/PII).
- Admin override visibility: Support-only UI (not in customer-facing Console) is out of scope for this design ticket; needs separate flow once ENG-5852 lands.

Acceptance criteria
- Wireframes cover list view + detail drawer + deep-link entry/return patterns.
- Includes at least: loading, empty, and error states.
- Copy is placeholder but respects length constraints; aligns with DES-427 tone.
- Reviewed with PM (Marissa/Nikhil), Eng (Dylan/Chloe), and DevEx sponsor (Alex) for MVP feasibility.

Handoff notes for engineering
- Drawer is intended as a reusable component (used for checklist steps now; could be used later for “recommended optimizations”).
- CTA prioritization: every step should have exactly one primary action; additional links are secondary.
- Telemetry hooks: each CTA click needs an analytics event (names TBD in event schema ticket; ensure wireframes indicate where tracking should be captured).

Links
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/guided-onboarding-first-production-launch-prd.json
- UX spec follow-up: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/onboarding-checklist-console-ux-spec.json
- Rollout/feature flag: PM-768
- Copy guidelines: DES-427

Outcome
Wireframes and prototype delivered; feedback incorporated from dogfood notes (confusing step order, missing deep link back to checklist) and engineering review (drawer component constraints). Final frames are ready for inclusion in the UX spec and for ENG-5814 implementation kickoff.
comments: 2025-02-10 — Marissa Cole: Entry point on Console Home makes sense for PLG. Please ensure we have a full-page view too; Home module alone won’t scale once we add more ‘production launch’ steps.
2025-02-11 — Dylan Brooks: Drawer pattern is good. Call out error states explicitly—progress service will occasionally 5xx during rollout; we need a user-safe failure mode (don’t block Console).

2025-02-12 — Kenji Nakamura: Added error + loading states and a neutral ‘Waiting for activity’ variant to address telemetry lag (users currently think Usage is broken). Updated prototype link with these flows.
2025-02-13 — Nikhil Sharma: Keep the first 3 steps oriented around getting a successful request; avoid putting quotas/budgets before first call. Move quotas/budgets under ‘Production launch’ section.

2025-02-14 — Dev Patel: Support request—when a step is in ‘Attention’ state, include top 2 troubleshooting bullets and link to the exact doc section. Biggest offenders: invalid API key, 429 surprises, streaming disconnect confusion.
2025-02-17 — Tessa Morgan: Copy length is trending long in the drawer. Please align to DES-427: one sentence ‘why it matters’, then bullets. Avoid marketing tone; keep it actionable.
2025-02-18 — Kenji Nakamura: Revised drawer layout to: Why (1 line), Completion criteria (bullets), Primary CTA, Troubleshooting accordion. Reduced description lengths to fit 2 lines in list view.
2025-02-20 — Logan Wright: For deep links, please make sure we can emit ‘checklist_cta_clicked’ with step_id and destination. Wireframes should label primary CTAs clearly (one per step).

2025-03-03 — George Mbatha: UX note from quick internal validation: users expect a ‘Back to checklist’ affordance when landing on an API Keys deep link. Inline banner is sufficient; no need for a tour overlay in MVP.

2025-03-18 — Kenji Nakamura: Marking Done. Final prototype includes inline banner return path, revised step ordering (first call first), and explicit data-lag microcopy on usage/telemetry-related steps. Ready for inclusion in the UX spec.
